shows.name: Managing Engineers
shows.tagline: Engineering leadership, the hard way and the good way.

episodes.title: Your first month as a manager
episodes.summary: What actually changes when you stop shipping code and start shipping people.

chapters.title: The promotion nobody prepares you for
What we'd tell our past selves

transcript.text: Welcome to Managing Engineers. This is the show about the job nobody trains you for.
Today we're talking about the first month, because that's where most of the damage gets done.
Nobody sits you down and says, congratulations, you're no longer measured on the thing you're good at.
The first instinct is to keep coding. It feels productive. It's also the quickest way to stall your team.
So the question becomes: what does a good week look like when you've shipped nothing yourself?
One-to-ones are the job. Not a meeting you squeeze between the real work.
Ask what's getting in the way. Then actually go and remove it.
Letting go of the keyboard is a grieving process. Be kind to yourself.
Your team's output is now your output. That's the whole shift.
If we could go back, we'd ask for help in week one, not month six.

episodes.title: Feedback that lands
episodes.summary: Giving direct feedback without bruising the person or the relationship.

transcript.text: Feedback. Everyone says they want it, and almost nobody gives it well.
We avoid it because we're worried about the relationship. Ironically, avoiding it is what damages the relationship.
Specific beats kind-but-vague every single time.
Here's the structure we keep coming back to: situation, behaviour, impact, and then a question.
The question matters. It turns a verdict into a conversation.
Sometimes it goes wrong anyway. Own it, say so, and try again next week.
